question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the highlighted group of words in the given sentence.

We went to Bowbazaar in Kolkata to see the buildings for the lodging and accommodation of soldiers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. barracks.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Barracks" means a building or group of buildings used for the lodging and accommodation of soldiers. (सैनिकों के रहने का स्थान / बैरक)

◦ Correct: We went to Bowbazaar in Kolkata to see the barracks.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "paddocks" — small enclosed fields where horses are kept or exercised.

• Option 3 "hostels" — buildings providing inexpensive lodging, usually for students or travellers, not specifically soldiers.

• Option 4 "mints" — places where coins/currency are manufactured.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: cantonment (a military station/town), garrison (troops stationed to defend a place), arsenal (a store of weapons), armoury (a place where arms are kept).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The company decided / to phase up its / outdated technology / and embrace innovation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. to phase up its.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct phrasal verb is "phase out", which means to gradually stop using or withdraw something. "Phase up" is not a standard phrasal verb; since the technology is "outdated", it must be discontinued, i.e., "phased out". (धीरे-धीरे समाप्त करना)

◦ Correct: The company decided to phase out its outdated technology and embrace innovation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "The company decided", "outdated technology" and "and embrace innovation" are all grammatically correct segments.

• "Phase in" is the opposite phrasal verb — to gradually introduce something new.

NOTE

• Useful phrasal verbs for SSC: phase out (discontinue gradually), phase in (introduce gradually), do away with (abolish), wipe out (destroy completely).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Fabricate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Construct.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fabricate" means to make, build or construct something; it can also mean to invent false information. Its closest synonym here is "construct" (to build or put together). (निर्माण करना / गढ़ना)

◦ Example: The workers fabricated/constructed the steel framework in a week.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Garments" (clothes) is a noun and unrelated.

• Option 3 "Fascinate" means to attract or charm greatly.

• Option 4 "Floral" (relating to flowers) is an adjective and unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of fabricate: construct, manufacture, build, assemble; (in the sense of lying) invent, concoct, forge. Antonyms: demolish, destroy, dismantle.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Fantastic
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Fanciful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fantastic" means imaginative, fanciful, strange or existing only in the imagination; informally it also means wonderful. Its closest synonym is "fanciful" (based on imagination rather than reality). (काल्पनिक / विलक्षण)

◦ Example: The novel is full of fantastic/fanciful creatures and imaginary lands.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Practical" (realistic, sensible) is nearly an antonym of fantastic.

• Option 3 "Graceful" (elegant in movement) and Option 4 "Delicate" (fragile, fine) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of fantastic: fanciful, imaginary, fabulous, whimsical, unreal. Antonyms: real, practical, ordinary, realistic.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence.

You must adhere to the rules of this place.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Comply.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Adhere to" means to follow, obey or stick to (rules, beliefs or instructions). Its closest synonym is "comply (with)" — to act in accordance with rules or requests. (पालन करना)

◦ Example: All employees must adhere to/comply with the safety regulations.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Strict" (severe) is an adjective, not a verb.

• Option 3 "Remember" (to recall) and Option 4 "Aware" (having knowledge) do not convey the sense of obeying rules.

NOTE

• Synonyms of adhere (to rules): comply, abide by, observe, obey, conform. Antonyms: violate, disobey, flout, breach. "Adhere" literally also means "to stick firmly" (like glue).

question:
Select the most appropriate adjective to fill in the blank.

After coming from a long journey he said, “It feels so _________ to be home”.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. good.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After verbs of sensation like "feel", we use an adjective in the positive degree when no comparison is being made. "It feels so good to be home" is the natural, correct expression. (अच्छा लगना)

◦ Correct: "It feels so good to be home."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "better" (comparative) and Option 4 "best" (superlative) are wrong because no comparison is intended, and "so" is followed by the positive degree.

• Option 3 "much good" is unidiomatic; "so much good" cannot qualify "feels" here.

NOTE

• Linking verbs (feel, seem, look, taste, smell, sound) are followed by adjectives, not adverbs: "It feels good", "She looks happy", "The soup tastes delicious".

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A word, number, or other figure that looks the same when viewed (or rotated) upside down.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Ambigram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "ambigram" is a word, number or figure that reads the same (or as another word) when viewed or rotated upside down, e.g., the word "SWIMS" looks the same when turned upside down. (उलटा करने पर भी वैसा ही दिखने वाला शब्द/आकृति)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Anadiplosis" — a rhetorical device where the last word of one clause begins the next clause.

• Option 2 "Alliteration" — repetition of the same initial sound in nearby words (e.g., "she sells sea shells").

• Option 3 "Anagram" — a word formed by rearranging the letters of another word (e.g., "listen" → "silent").

NOTE

• Related terms: palindrome — a word/number that reads the same backwards and forwards (e.g., MADAM, 121); anagram — rearrangement of letters; ambigram — same when rotated/flipped.

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

The sports teacher saw across the game and punished the students who were cheating in the game.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. through.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "see through" means to detect the true nature of something; to not be deceived by a trick. The teacher "saw through the game" — i.e., he detected the students' trick/deception. (चाल को भाँप लेना)

◦ Correct: The sports teacher saw through the game and punished the students who were cheating.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "See across", "see underneath", "see beside" and "see beneath" are not idiomatic in the sense of detecting deception.

• "Game" here figuratively means a trick or secret plan.

NOTE

• Useful "see" phrasal verbs: see through (detect a trick / support till the end), see off (bid farewell), see to (attend to), see about (deal with).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Squadroun.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Squadroun" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "squadron", meaning a unit of an air force, army cavalry or naval fleet. (स्क्वाड्रन — वायु सेना/सेना की टुकड़ी)

• Spelling key: SQUAD + RON (no "u" before the final "n").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Vigilante" (a person who takes the law into his own hands), "masquerade" (a false show; a masked ball) and "caricature" (a comically exaggerated portrait) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Commonly confused military words: squadron (air force unit), battalion (army unit), regiment, platoon. Watch the double letters and silent vowels in such words.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Piquant
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Bland.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Piquant" means having a pleasantly sharp, spicy or stimulating taste/flavour. Its antonym is "bland", meaning tasteless, mild or lacking flavour. (चटपटा का विलोम — फीका)

◦ Example: The piquant chutney was served with rather bland rice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Bitter" is itself a strong taste, not the opposite of "sharp/spicy".

• Options 3 "Delicious" and 4 "Delectable" (both meaning very tasty) are closer to synonyms in spirit, not antonyms.

NOTE

• Synonyms of piquant: spicy, tangy, zesty, pungent, savoury. Antonyms: bland, insipid, flavourless, tasteless.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Choronology.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Choronology" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "chronology", meaning the arrangement of events in the order in which they occurred. (कालक्रम)

• Spelling key: CHRONO (time) + LOGY (study) — from Greek "chronos" = time; there is no "o" between "ch" and "r".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Competent" (capable), "soliloquy" (speaking one's thoughts aloud when alone, as in drama) and "protein" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Words from "chronos" (time): chronology, chronic, chronicle, synchronise, anachronism. Note "protein" follows the exception to "i before e except after c".

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error in the usage of indefinite articles.

We have invited / our friends / for a / dinner.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. for a.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Names of meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner, supper) do not take an article when used in a general sense. So "invited our friends for dinner" is correct — the indefinite article "a" must be removed. (भोजन के नामों से पहले article नहीं लगता)

◦ Correct: We have invited our friends for dinner.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "We have invited", "our friends" and "dinner" are correct segments.

• An article is used with a meal only when it is qualified by an adjective: "a delicious dinner", "a grand lunch".

NOTE

• Article rules with meals: "have breakfast/lunch/dinner" (no article), but "a hearty breakfast", "the dinner hosted by the President" (specific).

question:
Select the idiom that can substitute the bracketed word segment correctly and complete the given sentence meaningfully.

The negotiations reached a point where both parties had to (confront the consequences of their actions) and make tough decisions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. face the music.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "face the music" means to confront the unpleasant consequences of one's actions; to accept criticism or punishment. (अपने कर्मों के परिणाम भुगतना)

◦ Correct: ... both parties had to face the music and make tough decisions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "break a leg" — good luck (said before a performance).

• Option 3 "cut corners" — to do something cheaply or carelessly, skipping steps.

• Option 4 "get cold feet" — to become nervous and back out at the last moment.

NOTE

• Similar idioms: "pay the piper", "reap what you sow", "take it on the chin" — all involve accepting consequences.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Mohan is still confused about his higher studies.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. No error.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Mohan is still confused about his higher studies." is grammatically correct — subject (Mohan) + verb (is) + adverb (still) + adjective (confused) + preposition (about) + object (his higher studies).

• "Confused about" is the correct adjective + preposition combination.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Mohan is still" — correct placement of the adverb "still" between the auxiliary and the adjective.

• "his higher studies" — correct possessive usage; "higher studies" is a standard expression for advanced education.

NOTE

• Common adjective + preposition pairs: confused about, good at, afraid of, interested in, satisfied with, responsible for. Errors in such pairs are frequently tested in SSC exams.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Postuer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Postuer" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "posture", meaning the position in which a person holds his body while standing or sitting. (शारीरिक मुद्रा)

• Spelling key: POS + TURE — it ends in "-ture" like the other options.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Gesture" (a movement of the hand/head to express an idea), "culture" (customs and way of life) and "lecture" (an educational talk) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Words ending in "-ture": posture, gesture, culture, lecture, nature, picture, capture, mixture, furniture. The "-ture" ending is pronounced /chər/.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.

My old car was pressed into service as an emergency vehicle for my ailing grandmother.
option_3: To use for a particular purpose when a special need occurs.
option_4: Used to take someone to the hospital
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To use for a particular purpose when a special need occurs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "pressed into service" means to be made to serve or be used for a purpose, usually in an emergency or when a special need arises. (आवश्यकता पड़ने पर काम में लाना)

◦ In the sentence, the old car was used in an emergency to help the ailing grandmother.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 4 describe literal or narrow situations, not the general idiomatic meaning of using something because of a sudden need.

NOTE

• Related expressions: "call into service", "bring into play", "make do with" (use whatever is available). "Press" here means to force into use.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Ramya would gladly help Manya if you had asked her.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. would have gladly helped.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The if-clause "if you had asked her" is in the past perfect, so the sentence is a third conditional (unreal past). The main clause must take "would have + past participle (V3)" — "would have gladly helped". (तृतीय conditional)

◦ Correct: Ramya would have gladly helped Manya if you had asked her.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "is to gladly help" and Option 2 "will gladly help" refer to present/future and clash with "had asked".

• Option 3 "was to have gladly helped" is not the standard conditional structure.

NOTE

• Conditional patterns: First — If + present, will + V1; Second — If + past, would + V1; Third — If + past perfect, would have + V3 (for imagined past situations).

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options.
option_1: The hard disc of a computer on a desk needs to be repaired at the earliest.
option_2: A hard disc of the computer on the desk needs to be repaired at the earliest.
option_3: The hard disc of the computer on the desk needs to be repaired at the earliest.
option_4: The hard disc of a computer on the desk needs to be repaired at an earliest.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The hard disc of the computer on the desk needs to be repaired at the earliest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• We are speaking of a specific hard disc of a specific computer on a specific desk, so the definite article "the" is required before all three nouns: "The hard disc of the computer on the desk".

• The fixed phrase is "at the earliest" (as soon as possible), never "at an earliest".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 wrongly uses "a computer on a desk" (indefinite) though a particular computer is meant.

• Option 2 wrongly uses "A hard disc" for the specific disc.

• Option 4 wrongly says "at an earliest".

NOTE

• "The" is used for things already identified or made specific by a phrase like "of the computer/on the desk". Superlatives also take "the": at the earliest, at the latest, the best.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Gregarious
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Sociable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gregarious" means fond of company; enjoying being with other people; sociable. (मिलनसार)

◦ Example: A gregarious/sociable person makes friends easily at parties.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Isolated" (alone, separated), Option 3 "Introverted" (inward-looking, shy) and Option 4 "Reserved" (not revealing feelings, quiet) are all antonyms of gregarious.

• "Gregarious" is also used of animals that live in flocks or herds.

NOTE

• Synonyms of gregarious: sociable, outgoing, extroverted, affable, convivial. Antonyms: introverted, reserved, unsociable, reclusive.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The manager had / thrown up the / drunk people sitting / inside his office premises.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. thrown up the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct phrasal verb is "throw out", meaning to expel or force someone to leave a place. "Throw up" means to vomit, which is absurd here. So it should be "had thrown out the drunk people". (बाहर निकालना)

◦ Correct: The manager had thrown out the drunk people sitting inside his office premises.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "The manager had", "drunk people sitting" and "inside his office premises" are grammatically acceptable segments.

NOTE

• "Throw" phrasal verbs: throw out (expel/discard), throw up (vomit / produce hastily), throw away (discard), throw off (get rid of), throw in (add free of cost).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Man, it would seem, has (1)______ from arboreal apes. They lived a happy life in tropical forests, eating coconuts when they were hungry, and throwing them at each other when they were not. They were (2)______ occupied in gymnastics and acquired an (3)______ which to us is truly (4)______. But after some millions of years of this arboreal paradise, their numbers increased to the point where the supply of coconuts was no longer (5)________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. descended.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Descended from" means to have developed or evolved from an ancestor. The passage says man has evolved "descended from arboreal apes" (apes that live in trees). (वंशज होना)

◦ Correct: Man, it would seem, has descended from arboreal apes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "ascended" (climbed up), Option 3 "recommended" (suggested) and Option 4 "extended" (stretched) do not collocate with "from ... apes" in the sense of ancestry.

• "Arboreal" means living in trees (वृक्षवासी).

NOTE

• "Be descended from" is the fixed expression for lineage/evolution: "Birds are descended from dinosaurs." The noun is "descendant"; the antonym concept is "ancestor".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Man, it would seem, has (1)______ from arboreal apes. They lived a happy life in tropical forests, eating coconuts when they were hungry, and throwing them at each other when they were not. They were (2)______ occupied in gymnastics and acquired an (3)______ which to us is truly (4)______. But after some millions of years of this arboreal paradise, their numbers increased to the point where the supply of coconuts was no longer (5)________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. perpetually.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Perpetually" means constantly; all the time; without interruption. The apes were "perpetually occupied in gymnastics" — always busy swinging and climbing. (निरंतर / सदा)

◦ Correct: They were perpetually occupied in gymnastics ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "professionally" (as a profession) does not suit apes.

• Option 3 "bisectionally" is not a standard English word in this context.

• Option 4 "conspiratorially" (in a secretive, plotting manner) does not fit "occupied in gymnastics".

NOTE

• Synonyms of perpetually: constantly, continually, incessantly, eternally. The adjective is "perpetual" (a perpetual motion machine, perpetual snow).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Man, it would seem, has (1)______ from arboreal apes. They lived a happy life in tropical forests, eating coconuts when they were hungry, and throwing them at each other when they were not. They were (2)______ occupied in gymnastics and acquired an (3)______ which to us is truly (4)______. But after some millions of years of this arboreal paradise, their numbers increased to the point where the supply of coconuts was no longer (5)________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. agility.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Agility" means the ability to move quickly, easily and nimbly. Constant gymnastics would naturally give the apes "an agility which to us is truly astonishing". (फुर्ती)

◦ Correct: They were perpetually occupied in gymnastics and acquired an agility ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "civility" (politeness), Option 2 "density" (compactness) and Option 4 "variability" (tendency to change) cannot be acquired through gymnastics.

• Note the article "an" before the blank — it correctly precedes the vowel sound of "agility".

NOTE

• Synonyms of agility: nimbleness, quickness, dexterity, suppleness. The adjective is "agile" (an agile gymnast, an agile mind).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Man, it would seem, has (1)______ from arboreal apes. They lived a happy life in tropical forests, eating coconuts when they were hungry, and throwing them at each other when they were not. They were (2)______ occupied in gymnastics and acquired an (3)______ which to us is truly (4)______. But after some millions of years of this arboreal paradise, their numbers increased to the point where the supply of coconuts was no longer (5)________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. astonishing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Astonishing" means very surprising; amazing. The agility of the apes, when compared with human ability, is "truly astonishing" to us. (आश्चर्यजनक)

◦ Correct: ... acquired an agility which to us is truly astonishing.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "disappointing" (causing dissatisfaction), Option 2 "boring" (dull) and Option 4 "frightening" (causing fear) do not express admiration for remarkable agility.

NOTE

• Synonyms of astonishing: amazing, astounding, stunning, staggering, remarkable. The passage is adapted from Bertrand Russell's humorous prose on human evolution.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Man, it would seem, has (1)______ from arboreal apes. They lived a happy life in tropical forests, eating coconuts when they were hungry, and throwing them at each other when they were not. They were (2)______ occupied in gymnastics and acquired an (3)______ which to us is truly (4)______. But after some millions of years of this arboreal paradise, their numbers increased to the point where the supply of coconuts was no longer (5)________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. adequate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Adequate" means enough; sufficient for the need. As the apes' numbers increased, the supply of coconuts was "no longer adequate" — i.e., no longer enough for all of them. (पर्याप्त)

◦ Correct: ... their numbers increased to the point where the supply of coconuts was no longer adequate.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "deficient" (insufficient) would create a double negative with "no longer" and reverse the intended meaning.

• Option 2 "delicate" (fragile) and Option 4 "consecrate" (to declare sacred — a verb) do not fit.

NOTE

• Synonyms of adequate: sufficient, enough, satisfactory, ample. Antonyms: inadequate, deficient, insufficient, scanty. Watch out for "no longer + adjective" constructions — the adjective itself must be positive in sense.
